title: Azure SQL Database
description: Learn how Azure SQL Database provides a fully managed relational database with elastic pools, serverless compute, and hyperscale tiers.

data.text: Azure SQL Database is a fully managed relational database service built on the latest SQL Server engine. Microsoft handles backups, patching, high availability, and operating system maintenance. You focus on building your application and writing queries. The service runs as Platform as a Service (PaaS), which means you do not manage any virtual machines or physical hardware.

data.title: Fully Managed Means Less Ops Work
data.text: With Azure SQL Database, you never need to manually apply security patches, schedule backups, or configure failover. Azure performs these tasks automatically so your database stays healthy with minimal effort.

Azure SQL Database offers three main compute and storage configurations to match different workload patterns: General Purpose for most business applications, Business Critical for low-latency and high-throughput workloads, and Hyperscale for very large databases that need to scale beyond typical limits.

data.title: Common Compute Models
items: Provisioned compute: you reserve a fixed amount of CPU and memory.
Serverless compute: Azure automatically scales compute up and down and can pause the database during idle periods.
Elastic pools: share a pool of compute resources across multiple databases to reduce cost.
Hyperscale: separates compute from storage and supports very large databases up to hundreds of terabytes.

data.title: Provision Azure SQL Database with ARM Template
data.content: Deploy a serverless Azure SQL Database using an Azure Resource Manager JSON template.

data.text: An elastic pool is a collection of databases that share a set amount of compute and storage resources. Instead of provisioning each database separately, you buy a pool that serves multiple databases. This works well when databases have different usage patterns that do not all peak at the same time.

data.title: When to Use Elastic Pools
data.text: Elastic pools work best when your databases have complementary usage patterns. For example, a development database might be busy during work hours while a reporting database is busy overnight. Sharing a pool saves money compared to reserving individual resources for each database.

Serverless compute automatically scales the database based on workload demand. When there is no activity, Azure can pause the database and you only pay for storage. When a query arrives, Azure resumes the database within seconds. This is ideal for development, testing, or applications with irregular or unpredictable usage patterns.

data.title: Cold Start Latency
data.text: Resuming a paused serverless database takes a few seconds. If your application needs sub-second response times at all times, consider using provisioned compute instead of serverless.

Hyperscale is designed for very large databases that need to grow beyond the limits of standard Azure SQL tiers. It uses a page server architecture that separates compute from storage and supports rapid scaling. You can grow a Hyperscale database up to hundreds of terabytes without manually managing storage sharding.

terms.definition: Database Transaction Unit, a blended measure of CPU, memory, and IO that represents the power of an Azure SQL Database tier.
Virtual core, a more flexible pricing model that lets you choose the exact number of CPU cores and amount of memory.
A shared set of compute and storage resources that multiple databases can use, with auto-scaling within configured limits.
An Azure SQL tier that supports very large databases by separating compute from storage and using a distributed page server architecture.

data.title: Explore Azure SQL Database Options
data.description: Use the Azure Pricing Calculator to estimate the cost of a General Purpose, Serverless, and Hyperscale Azure SQL Database for a 100 GB database with 500 DTUs.
steps: Open the Azure Pricing Calculator at azure.microsoft.com/pricing/calculator.
Add the Azure SQL Database product.
Compare the monthly cost of General Purpose, Serverless, and Hyperscale tiers.
Note the differences in compute model, storage limits, and included features.
data.expectedOutcome: You can explain the cost and feature differences between General Purpose, Serverless, and Hyperscale tiers and identify which tier fits a given workload.

data.title: Azure SQL Database at a Glance
points: Azure SQL Database is a fully managed PaaS relational database.
Elastic pools share compute across multiple databases to reduce cost.
Serverless compute auto-scales and can pause during idle periods.
Hyperscale supports very large databases with near-instant backup and rapid scale-out.
data.takeaway: Azure SQL Database removes infrastructure management while offering flexible compute tiers, from serverless dev/test workloads to massive Hyperscale production databases.
